title: Granular lock levels and pin-resolution playbook (tag / semver / commit-hash)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers need predictable, auditable model selection across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Current pin semantics are underspecified for multi-level locks (route/customer/team) and for mixed selector inputs (tag name vs semver range vs exact commit-hash). This ticket defines a playbook and the SDK/API changes required to: 1) make pin resolution deterministic and observable, 2) allow graceful degradation when exact pins are unavailable, and 3) bind performance profiles and published telemetry to immutable model artifacts.

Scope: Define semantics for three selector types (tag alias, semver range, commit-hash), describe precedence across lock levels (route > project > customer > global), specify runtime fallback rules and a migration CLI for customers to convert tags/aliases to hashes. Include acceptance criteria, rollout plan, SDK surface changes (resolution API and diagnostic headers), and required console and docs updates.
acceptance_criteria: API change doc: /v1/models resolution endpoint documents precedence and resolution algorithm (tag, semver, hash) and is reviewed
SDKs (python/js/go) expose ModelPin.resolve(pin, context) that returns: resolved_hash, provenance (route|customer|global), and resolution_path
Runtime: when a pinned hash is unavailable, runtime attempts configured fallbacks in documented order and emits X-Model-Pin-Trace header with trace token
Performance profile publishing tied to immutable hash: console shows per-hash perf metrics and flags regressions when profile deviates >5% latency or >2% quality drop
Migration CLI: redwood pin-migrate --from-tag TAG --to-hash HASH --dry-run produces non-destructive preview and an audit log entry
E2E tests: unit and integration tests cover resolution permutations and fallback behavior across hosted/dedicated/private modes
Security: KMS/HSM secrets not exposed in resolution payloads; security review sign-off obtained

implementation_notes: Key decisions: 1) Precedence order = route override -> project pin -> customer pin -> org default -> global default. 2) Selector semantics: exact commit-hash matches single artifact; tag resolves to latest published hash for that alias (with stability window configurable per-customer); semver range resolves to the highest semver-satisfying hash published within retention window. 3) Telemetry: resolution_path and resolved_hash emitted as metadata in trace events and as X-Model-Pin-Trace header for debugging; full provenance sent to internal logs only (redacted in user-facing UI). 4) Fallback policy: configurable per-route with modes {strict, best-effort, degrade-to-closest-profile}. 5) Performance profiles must be published against immutable hash; publishing UI will require explicit 'confirm bind to hash' checkbox.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer relies on floating tags -> may get unexpected behavior after tie-breaker changes. Mitigation: migration CLI and dry-run preview, plus email notice and one-month opt-in freeze window.
Risk: Semver metadata inconsistent across publishers. Mitigation: validate semver fields at upload and surface warnings in console; treat invalid semver as non-candidate for range resolution.
Risk: Rollout across Dedicated/Private could diverge. Mitigation: ship resolution algorithm as config flag and default to safe behavior; compatibility tests against on-prem images.
